name: The Atelier
alt: Studio suite with bed, desk, and natural light
lead: A single volume where the desk faces the window and the bed sits behind a low oak screen — built for the resident who works where they sleep and refuses to feel it.
body: The desk is 140 cm of solid oak with a dedicated circuit, so a monitor, a laptop dock and a lamp run without a single extension lead crossing the floor.
Storage is vertical rather than wide: a full-height wardrobe and a shallow shelf run above the bed, which keeps the floor clear and the room reading larger than its 28 square metres.
North-facing glazing means indirect light all day and no afternoon heat load on the desk.

name: The Reader
alt: One-bedroom suite with separate sitting area and tall windows
lead: A separate bedroom behind a solid door, and a sitting room with a wall built for shelves — the plan for a resident who wants the day and the night to be different rooms.
body: The bedroom door is a solid core, not a hollow panel: measured at the door line, the sitting room television at normal volume drops to a level you can sleep through.
The long wall carries a continuous shelf run at 2.4 m — the only wall in the building specified without electrical boxes so it can be filled end to end.
The sitting room takes a two-metre sofa and a dining table for four at the same time without either blocking the window.

name: The Salon
alt: Corner suite with lounge seating and double-aspect windows
lead: The corner plan — double aspect, a dining table that seats six, and the only suite in the building where you can have people over without moving the furniture first.
body: Two exposures mean cross-ventilation: with both windows open the room turns over its air without the air-conditioning running, which matters most in the hours after sunset.
The kitchen is open to the dining end rather than shut in a galley, so cooking for six is a conversation rather than an exile.
The corner column is boxed into joinery, not left proud — the plan reads as one room, not a rectangle with a bite taken out of it.
